analysis: Integration of four units. The PR adds .github/workflows/ci-dev-hourly.yml (head lines 1-38), a changelog fragment, docs/developer/build.md additions, and scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py changes (HOURLY constant, classification set, test_hourly_full_run_only_dispatches_ci_dev_on_dev). The workflow file was verified directly from replayed source. It triggers on schedule and workflow_dispatch only, has top-level permissions {}, and a single ubuntu-24.04 job with actions: write and contents: read. It has no checkout, no uses:, no secrets, and no id-token. GH_TOKEN and REPOSITORY come from github.token and github.repository via env, not interpolated into the shell script, so there is no injection path. The only side effect is `gh workflow run ci-dev.yml --repo "$REPOSITORY" --ref dev`, guarded by an unfinished-run check. Scheduled runs execute only from the default branch. workflow_dispatch requires write access, which already permits dispatching ci-dev.yml directly, so no new privilege is created. The new test pins these constraints (no uses/secrets/checkout/id-token/self-hosted/darkbloom- labels, a single dispatch command), so it tightens CI governance and weakens no existing check. The change does not touch provider code, coordinator contract, attestation, keys, cache storage, or release signing, so TB-002/003/007/009/011-014, A-001..A-020 and T-041 are unaffected. Unverified contract: dev's ci-dev.yml must accept workflow_dispatch, select all components, and file the failure issue. That lives on the dev branch and is outside the evidence. If it is missing, the result is an HTTP 422 job failure, which is an availability/CI-coverage concern, not a security regression. Dispatched runs may use the routed Darkbloom runners, but how ci-dev.yml handles dispatch-time runner routing and cache saves is outside this PR and was not examined. Nine replayed units were omitted from the integration source, but the reviewed workflow and test content is complete for the changed security-relevant files. No findings.
